key_concepts: Like magnetic poles repel each other.
Magnets can attract iron filings and separate them from non-magnetic mixtures.
A compass can be used to identify the north and south poles of a magnet.
Iron filings sprinkled around a magnet reveal its magnetic field pattern.
Magnetic field shapes vary with magnet shape.
Objects attracted to magnets are usually made of iron or steel.
Rubbing a nail with a magnet in one direction can magnetize the nail.
Knocking a magnetized nail can demagnetize it.
An electric current flowing through a coil produces a magnetic field.
Reversing the battery connections reverses the coil's magnetic poles.
An electromagnet cannot pick up magnetic objects when the current is disconnected.
Increasing the number of coils or changing battery size can change electromagnet strength.
